payload.goal: A fresh session should open on the initiative the last session actually finished in, without any surface guessing. Resolution stays branch-first (session-orientation D2 stands); what changes is that the branch binding stops being a fact only a human command maintains. sofar_end_session binds the current branch to the session's home, so bindings.json becomes a durable, inspectable record of last-worked instead of decaying the moment work moves — brillo's main stayed bound to baseui-toast-migration across 8 project-tax-architecture commits, and every fresh session there started on the wrong record.

payload.because: The user's instinct — "last initiative a session finished in, discounting live peers" — is right, and this delivers exactly that answer while computing none of it. A live peer has not ended, so it never moves the binding; the branch therefore names the last CONCLUDED work, which is what "open on what I was last working on" means. (b) cannot be built honestly: sibling liveness is not knowable from the record. fold.ts:927 already says so in the codebase's own words, that a sibling with no session_closed "might be a crashed process that would linger as a false conflict forever", and this repo proves it empirically — four sessions are open without write-back right now (6efd8ee9, 2b0bd269, 7e56a4a0, 74e0b536). Resolution built on that signal degrades every time a session crashes. (a) is settled by D2 and nothing here reopens it: resolveBound feeds handlePostTool and every other hook, so redirecting resolution moves where events LAND, and this changes no resolution code at all. Read-time inference also loses on three counts a write-time fact wins: it is invisible, where `cat .sofar/bindings.json` states exactly what the next session gets; it is unoverridable, where `sofar switch` beats a binding permanently; and it costs a per-hook scan of N logs, where session-orientation 2.3 measured 1.7ms for 38 initiatives on the SessionStart path alone and brillo has 59. (c) is refuted by the session that took this decision: it re-homed drift-certification to session-orientation purely to diagnose the report, and a re-home-time rebind would have pointed this repo's main at a CLOSED record. Write-back time also keeps the tree clean — bindings.json is committed, so the rebind lands inside the write-back moment and is committed with the record, obeying the protocol's write-back-then-commit order rather than leaving trailing dirt. Move-only rather than create because an unbound branch is a deliberate state in this repo (session-orientation itself was created with --no-bind so a peer's branch resolution would not move), and a fresh session on an unbound branch already gets a clear "not bound to an initiative" block telling it to switch. Evidence this is worth building: brillo's main stayed bound to baseui-toast-migration across 8 project-tax-architecture commits, so every fresh session there opened on the wrong record and needed the same manual re-home. Known limitation, accepted: with several peers on one branch the last to write back wins, so the binding becomes "most recently finished" rather than "correct". That is strictly better than weeks-stale, it cannot tear a live peer because homeInitiative treats the branch slug only as a seed candidate that any strictly later session_started displaces (mcp/context.ts:194), and session-orientation's notice remains the backstop for exactly that residue. Reverses the property test/rehome.test.ts pins at line 208-211, but narrowly: re-homing still touches nothing, and that test's own case still passes untouched because the peer's home IS the branch's record.
payload.chose: Make the branch binding self-maintaining at write-back time: sofar_end_session, after appending session_ended, binds the current branch to the initiative the write-back landed in. Three guards. It only MOVES a binding that already exists, so a branch deliberately left unbound (sofar new --no-bind) stays unbound. It skips a home whose initiative is closed or dropped. It is best-effort — a detached HEAD, a missing or malformed bindings.json, any throw at all leaves the write-back untouched. The rebind is reported back to the caller as an optional `rebound` field on the result, omitted when nothing moved, following the parallel_writebacks precedent.
payload.over: Three alternatives, all rejected. (a) Redirecting a fresh session's RESOLUTION to the most recently active initiative — the user's first framing, and session-orientation D2's rejected option (a). (b) The user's refinement of (a): detect whether parallel sessions are running and prefer the last initiative a session finished in, computed at read time. (c) Binding at RE-HOME time inside sofar_start_session rather than at write-back. Also rejected: leaving it alone and relying on sofar switch, and adding a statusline marker for the mismatch instead of fixing the underlying fact.
payload.rule: sofar_end_session binds the current branch to the session's home — MOVING an existing binding only, never creating one, and never onto a closed or dropped record. Resolution itself stays branch-first: never infer a fresh session's record from recency or peer liveness.

tasks.title: Implement the rebind in mcp/end-session.ts: after the session_ended append, bind the current branch to the write-back's slug via core/bindings writeBinding. Guards per D1 — move-only (skip when the branch has no existing binding), skip closed or dropped homes, skip a detached HEAD, and swallow every throw so a malformed bindings.json can never fail a write-back.

Report it: optional `rebound` field on EndSessionResult naming branch, from and to, omitted when nothing moved. Follows the parallel_writebacks precedent — the whole argument for a binding over an inference is that it is inspectable, so the act that moves it must be legible at the moment it happens.

Tests: the binding moves on write-back, does not move for a peer whose home IS the branch, is not CREATED on an unbound branch, is not moved onto a closed record, survives a malformed bindings.json, and leaves a live peer's own resolution untouched. Extend test/rehome.test.ts's header property rather than deleting it — re-homing still touches nothing; only the write-back binds.

docs/SPEC.md: state the rebind in the same passage that carries the re-homing contract and the session-before-branch precedence, including the move-only and closed-record guards and the new result field.

Gates: npm run typecheck, npm test, biome clean. Then dogfood against a scratch copy of the brillo record shape — bound main plus a home elsewhere — and confirm a following fresh session resolves to the finished record with no notice fired.

OPTIONAL, decide first: have the recent-work notice prefer a candidate whose newest event is a session_ended over one mid-flight, so it points at concluded work rather than a peer's live edit. Offered to the user and not yet accepted — decide before building, and drop it if the rebind alone makes the notice quiet enough.

Cut the release carrying this plus the two already-unreleased commits (cbcb391, 32a48d9). Peer obligation from plan-carry-forward: re-run sofar doctor from the INSTALLED build and diff byte-for-byte against 0.28.0 across every record — that comparison is what proves their fold change safe. payload.summary: Built and proved the rebind. Phases 1 and 2 closed, 5/5 tasks. The session began as a bug report — "new sessions do not inherit the last opened initiative" — and the first finding was that nothing was broken: session-orientation's notice fired in the exact session the user screenshotted (brillo transcript f15e6b7e, 16:02:03Z), it ships in 0.28.0, and brillo's protocol blocks are current. The real gap was that the notice never moves resolution while the statusline reads bindings.json, which only a human sofar switch ever maintained. D1 records the design and the three rejected alternatives, including the user's own refinement of resolving by peer liveness, which cannot be built honestly because sibling liveness is not knowable from the record. Implementation is rebindBranch in mcp/end-session.ts, called after the append and reusing the fold that overlappingWritebacks already needed. The result gains an optional rebound field. Gates: typecheck clean, biome clean, vitest 1688 passed and 4 skipped across 99 files. Dogfooded through the BUILT binary over stdio JSON-RPC, not only in-process: a scratch repo shaped like brillo rebound both ways and a following session-start opened on the rebound record with no notice line. One thing to know about this session's own write-back: the MCP server serving it is the installed 0.28.0, which has no rebind, so this repo's main is still bound to drift-certification and no peer's branch moved under them.
